To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HF-PSF is an increasingly common condition in primary care, with a poor prognosis and limited evidence base to inform its diagnosis and management.

1) HF-PSF is a distinct clinical entity, with a poor prognosis, 2) HF-PSFs are commonly underdiagnosed and undertreated in primary care, 3) the management of HF-PSFs is complex, and 4) multidisciplinary teams are required to deliver optimal care for patients with HF-PSF.

there is insufficient evidence to support the management of HF-PS in primary care.

the management of CHF with reduced systolic function is relatively well established in the literature.

The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need for a better understanding of the pathophysiology of HF-PS and a need to develop a better understanding of how to manage this common form of heart failure in the primary care setting.
primary care physicians need to be aware of the rising incidence of CHF in the community, and to be able to recognise the different presentations of CHF.
primary care practitioners should be encouraged to develop a higher index of suspicion for HF-PSF and to be familiar with the evidence in support its management.
